transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jorge Ramirez (CTO - Riverview), Priya Singh (Head of Security - Riverview), Evan Cole (Platform Eng), Maya Brooks (Product)

Summary:
[00:00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros. I'm Lena, AE on the account, Marcus is our SE.  Um Jorge, Priya, Evan, Maya thanks for making time.
[00:00:20] Jorge Ramirez: Sure thanks Lena. We've been talking with procurement and security so wanted to align on the pilot scope, especially the security controls.
[00:00:36] Marcus Li: Great. Our goal today is to nail success criteria, sizing for your expected workload, and run a benchmark that demonstrates latency/cost under your real-ish traffic. We'll also cover SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS and VPC connectivity. A lot to cover so we'll go high level then dive in.

Topics & qualification
[00:01:10] Maya Brooks: For context, our initial use case is clinical note summarization and triage routing, about 2000 notes/day, average note length ~1.2k tokens, peak concurrent requests ~25. We want sub-800ms 95th percentile generation time for short summaries.
[00:01:45] Evan Cole: Platform side we need SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; audit logs retained for minimum 1 year. Also data residency in us-east required, and KMS-backed encryption for any private deployment.
[00:02:10] Priya Singh: SOC 2 Type II is must-have, ISO 27001 is preferred. We need to validate RBAC controls, session logs, and have proof of encryption at rest with customer-managed keys ideally.
[00:02:35] Marcus Li: Understood. For the POC we commonly provide a Private pilot (VPC or private control plane) or Dedicated isolated pool. For security checks we can run with customer-managed KMS and SAML integration; audit logs are configurable and we can export to your SIEM.

Workload sizing & benchmarks
[00:05:00] Marcus Li: To size the POC we'll run a 2-hour benchmark with a mix of short and long prompts mirroring your 2000/day profile. We'll include KV/prefix cache warmup, and measure cost/tokens, latency p50/p95/p99, and any failure modes under load.
[00:05:30] Jorge Ramirez: Can you show cost delta between hosted vs dedicated with quantization? We need to justify spend if we go production.
[00:05:50] Marcus Li: We'll include a comparison sheet. For the POC we can spin a dedicated small GPU pool for the run; that isolates variance. Note transcriptions sometimes say 'quantization' as 'quanta zation' in our notes, so ignore that.

Security controls details
[00:08:10] Priya Singh: For SOC 2 we need Redwood's latest report and any exceptions. For ISO we need scope and certificate. Also ask: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model weights and logs?
[00:08:40] Lena Park: Yes, we can support KMS for data at rest and key management integrations; HSM is available for Private deployments. I'll attach our SOC 2 attestation and ISO summary in the security pack.
[00:09:05] Lena Park: Quick note: our SOC2 report is redacted for customer-specific info but includes control descriptions and auditor sign-off. We also provide SOC 2 mapping to common control frameworks.
[00:09:30] Priya Singh: Audit log retention - can we set 12+ month retention and forward events to Splunk or S3?
[00:09:45] Marcus Li: Yes, audit logs can be exported to your SIEM/S3 with configurable retention. We'll capture token-level metadata, API keys used, user id, model route, and more. There's a small storage cost which we'll call out.

SSO/SAML & RBAC
[00:11:20] Evan Cole: SAML metadata, do you support IdP-initiated SSO and SCIM for provisioning groups/roles? We want role-based access so only certain users can call production endpoints.
[00:11:40] Marcus Li: We support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, SAML 2.0.; SCIM for user/group provisioning is in the enterprise console. RBAC supports role templates (admin, developer, read-only) and can be mapped to SAML groups.
[00:12:02] Maya Brooks: Is there audit trail for RBAC changes?
[00:12:10] Marcus Li: Yes, all RBAC changes are logged with who changed what and when; those logs are part of audit export.

Network & private connectivity
[00:14:00] Jorge Ramirez: On network side we prefer VPC peering or Private deployment options. Can Redwood run on our VPC or do you require peering?
[00:14:20] Lena Park: We have options: VPC peering, Private (customer-owned control plane with on-prem option), or dedicated peered instances. For the POC we recommend VPC peering for easiest setup; Private full deployment would come later.

Success criteria and timeline
[00:17:20] Marcus Li: Let's define success criteria for the pilot. Proposed: 1) Security: SOC2 review completed, SAML integrated, KMS test passed; 2) Performance: 95th pct latency <800ms for short summaries under benchmark load; 3) Cost: demonstrate 20-30% improvement vs baseline (your current system) or clear path; 4) Integration: ability to export logs to your SIEM and set RBAC rules. Thoughts?
[00:18:05] Jorge Ramirez: That looks right. Would like explicit go/no-go gates after benchmark and security acceptance.
[00:18:20] Priya Singh: Security gating: SOC2 docs reviewed and one live KMS-backed test, SAML ok'd, and audit logs confirmed running to our SIEM.
[00:18:34] Lena Park: Timeline wise we propose: week 0 (this week) collect SAML metadata + traffic profile, week 1-2 infra setup, week 3 benchmark runs and iterative tuning, week 4-6 extended validation + handoff. So roughly 6 weeks end-to-end for the pilot.
[00:19:05] Evan Cole: That aligns with our internal timeline conditional on procurement and legal review.

Questions & objections
[00:20:00] Jorge Ramirez: How do you handle model updates and patching? We need to ensure no surprise regressions mid-pilot.
[00:20:20] Marcus Li: We pin model versions for the pilot. There's a rollback plan and can enable quality monitors. We'll run a small eval suite tied to your prompt sets to detect regressions.
[00:20:45] Priya Singh: Data residency - logs and traces must stay in us-east, can you guarantee that for the pilot?
[00:21:05] Lena Park: Yes, we can restrict storage and processing to us-east for pilot; we'll document data flow and sign off in the security packet.

Artifacts referenced
[00:22:00] Lena Park: I'll share security_pack_v3.pdf (SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM notes), benchmark_plan_template.xlsx, and a short onboarding checklist. Links will be in the follow-up email.

Recap & next steps
[00:24:00] Lena Park: Recap: We'll send the security pack by 8/22, Marcus will share benchmark plan by 8/28, Evan will provide SAML metadata and traffic profile by 8/25. We will schedule the 2-hour benchmark in the week of 8/31. Post-benchmark we reconvene for go/no-go.
[00:24:30] Jorge Ramirez: Sounds good. One more: any compliance for HIPAA? We are healthcare but pilot scope will avoid PHI; long-term we may need to evaluate HIPAA BAAs.
[00:24:55] Marcus Li: Short answer: we have HIPAA-capable deployments for Private options and BAAs for enterprise customers; that'll be a separate track but we can flag it now.

Closing
[00:25:30] Maya Brooks: Thanks all, we'll get the SAML and sample data over.
[00:25:40] Priya Singh: Thanks Lena, Marcus.
[00:25:45] Lena Park: Thanks team, we'll follow up with artifacts and next steps. Bye.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-labeling of speakers and small transcription errors; timestamps approximate.)
